properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean strata comprise Lower Carboniferous sandstones and siltstones of the Inverclyde Group, overlain by dense glacial till. Primary structural lithics consist of pale buff-grey quartz-arenite Craigleith sandstone ashlar, backed with Hailes sandstone rubble masonry. Bedding planes laid on natural quarry beds with non-hydraulic lime mortar pointing.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Mature urban parkland specimens: *Platanus × acerifolia* (London plane), *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), and *Tilia × europaea* (Common lime). State for late December: fully defoliated winter dormancy with bare branch ramification and exposed trunk bark.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical unified civic ensemble. Centerpiece: West Register House (former St George’s Church), featuring an advanced tetrastyle Ionic portico, stepped rusticated base, and a high circular peristyle drum supporting a ribbed copper dome and lantern. Flanked symmetrically by continuous 3-storey plus basement and attic Georgian residential terraces. Ground storeys feature channeled rustication; upper floors display polished ashlar with alternating pedimented and plain 6-over-6 timber sash-and-case windows. Foreground features the central Prince Albert Memorial equestrian bronze atop an elevated multi-tiered ashlar pedestal within an enclosed circular lawn.
